name: open-claude
description: A vim-style status bar in the Claude Code footer: editor mode, model, effort, cursor and usage.

lineNumbers.title: Number the draft's lines
lineNumbers.description: In the fullscreen renderer, draw each line's number over the two-cell gutter of the prompt box, in place of the prompt's own mark. Off leaves the gutter as Claude Code draws it.

minLines.title: Rows the prompt stands at the least
minLines.description: In the fullscreen renderer, keep the prompt box this many rows tall while its draft is shorter: blank rows are drawn under the draft and the box's rule under them. 1 leaves the box as Claude Code sizes it.

expandedLines.title: Rows the prompt stands at while expanded
expandedLines.description: In the fullscreen renderer, :expand (or /expand, which a key can be bound to as command:expand) stands the prompt box this many rows tall until the next prompt is sent, or until it is run again. Claude Code lets the box grow to half the screen less five rows, which is as tall as it stands with the default. Never fewer than minLines.

syntax.title: Color the draft's markdown
syntax.description: Paint the draft as it is typed: headings, emphasis, code, links, lists and quotes, and the code inside a fence by the language it names. The colors drop when the draft changes without a typed key (a new line from a rebound Enter, an edit in vim's normal mode) and return at the next one. Off leaves the draft as Claude Code draws it.

commandLine.title: A vim command line
commandLine.description: The focus chord for the area above the prompt (Ctrl+X Tab, or the key bound to abovePrompt:focus) opens a command line in the footer's last row: :w saves the draft for the session, :e loads it back, :q quits, each with its ! to force, :wq saves and quits, and any other name runs the slash command of that name. Enter runs the line and Escape leaves it. Off draws no field and keeps no drafts.

git.title: The git branch and the lines changed
git.description: Show, before the usage at the end of the footer, the branch the working copy is on and the lines added and deleted in its tracked files since the last commit, as git diff --numstat HEAD counts them. Read every five seconds and after each tool call.
